title: Game of Life with bounded or wrapped edges
instructions:
Implement `LifeGrid` and `neighbor_cells` in `life.py`. Coordinates are `(x, y)` integer pairs,
with `0 <= x < width` and `0 <= y < height`. Width and height are integers; wrap is a bool.
- `neighbor_cells(x, y, width, height, wrap=False) -> set[tuple[int, int]]` returns the
  distinct valid cells in the eight surrounding positions. In bounded mode discard off-grid
  positions. In wrapped mode reduce coordinates modulo the dimensions, deduplicate, and
  exclude the center cell itself. This matters for grids one or two cells wide/high.
  This helper receives valid dimensions and an in-bounds center.
- `LifeGrid(width, height, alive=(), wrap=False)` accepts an iterable of coordinate pairs.
  Duplicate live cells collapse. Nonpositive dimensions or an out-of-bounds live cell raise
  `ValueError`. Store public `width`, `height`, `wrap`, and `alive` (a `frozenset` of pairs).
  Copy input state; later mutation of the input collection must not affect the grid.
- `step() -> LifeGrid` returns a new grid with one simultaneous Conway step: live cells
  survive with two or three live neighbors; dead cells are born with exactly three.
- `advance(steps: int) -> LifeGrid` applies that many steps; negative steps raise `ValueError`.
  Zero returns a new grid with the same state.
Both methods preserve dimensions and wrap mode and never mutate the original grid.
